summary: David N. Keightley (1932–2017) was a sinologist and historian-archaeologist. He served as a professor at the University of California, Berkeley (attested in 1985 and 1999) and taught Imre Galambos.

David N. Lorenzen (b. 1940) specializes in Indology, history, archaeology, and religious studies. Educated at Wesleyan, SOAS, and the Australian National University under Arthur Llewellyn Basham, he served as a professor at El Colegio de México from 1970 to 2010.

David Ownby (b. 1958) works in sinology, religious studies, and history. After earning his B.A. from Vanderbilt and Ph.D. from Harvard (~1982–1989), he taught at Southern Methodist University and served as Professor of History at Université de Montréal (1994–2023).

David P. Chandler (b. 1933) is a historian who studied at Harvard, Yale, and the University of Michigan. Over his career, he held posts at Johns Hopkins, Cornell, the University of Wisconsin-Madison, and Monash University (~1972–1997).

David P. Jackson (b. 1951) is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned his degrees at the University of Washington, completing his Ph.D. under David Seyfort Ruegg, and served as a professor at the University of Hamburg (1992–2007).

David Patt is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He completed his Ph.D. at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (attested 1993) under the supervision of Geshe Lhundub Sopa, also studying with Geshe Lobsang Tenzin and Geshe Thubten Tandhar.

David Phillip Stanley specializes in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He earned his Ph.D. from the University of Virginia under Jeffrey Hopkins and David F. Germano, later serving as associate professor at Naropa University and Co-Director of the Nitartha Institute (attested 2019).

David Pingree (1933–2005) was an Indologist and historian. He earned his doctorate at Harvard (~1954–1960) under Daniel H. H. Ingalls and Otto Neugebauer, later holding professorships at the University of Chicago (1963–1971) and Brown University (appointed 1971).

David R. Kinsley (1939–2000) was a scholar of Indology and religious studies. He studied at Drew University, Union Theological Seminary, and the University of Chicago before serving on the faculty at McMaster University from 1969 to 2000.

David R. Loy (b. 1947) works in philosophy, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. After earning his doctorate at the National University of Singapore, he held faculty posts at Bunkyo University (1990–2006) and Xavier University (~2002–2010).

David Ralph Quinter is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Japanology. He completed his Ph.D. at Stanford University under Carl Bielefeldt and Bernard Faure, later becoming an associate professor of East Asian religions at the University of Alberta (attested 2019).

David Reigle (b. 1952) is an Indologist, Tibetologist, and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of California, Santa Barbara. He held a post at Asian Humanities Press (attested 2006).
David Ruddell (1943–2015) was a scholar in Indology and linguistics. He studied at Laval University and served as Secretary at Fort William College.

David Schaberg (b. 1964) is a sinologist who studied at Stanford and completed his Ph.D. at Harvard. Since 1996, he has held posts at the University of California, Los Angeles, including dean of Humanities (2012) and senior dean (2020).

David Seyfort Ruegg (1931–2021) specialized in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology, studying at the École Pratique des Hautes Études. His main academic posts included professorships at Leiden University (1966–1972), the University of Hamburg (1983–1990), and SOAS (~1993–2000).

David Shea (1777–1836) was a scholar of Iranian and Central Asian studies, linguistics, and Indology. Educated at Trinity College Dublin (1793), he served as Assistant Professor of Oriental Languages at East India Company College until 1836.

David Shulman (b. 1949) is an Indologist who earned his Ph.D. at SOAS, University of London under John Ralston Marr. He spent his career at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem, serving as professor and director (1992–1998).
David Slakter is a scholar in Indology and philosophy. He completed his master's degree at the University of Liverpool under the supervision of Christopher Bartley (degree completed by 2012).
David Steindl-Rast (b. 1926) is a religious studies scholar. He completed his studies at the University of Vienna and the Academy of Fine Arts Vienna between ~1945 and 1952.

David Tracy (1939–2025) was a scholar of religious studies and philosophy. After earning his doctorate at the Pontifical Gregorian University, he taught at Catholic University of America (1967–1969) and the University of Chicago Divinity School (~1969–2006).
